education_auth_register.learn: Creating an account gives you a place to stand — nothing more and nothing less. It does not make you a resident, and it never decides whether you may vote.
education_auth_register.s1_detail: Your account is yours alone. You can use a name nobody can trace to you — the app is built for pseudonyms.
education_auth_register.s1_do: Enter an email and a password
education_auth_register.s2_detail: You are now R-01 (Individual). You can look around everything public and file the handful of forms about yourself.
education_auth_register.s3_detail: Entirely optional, and always editable. No profile choice ever unlocks or blocks a right.
education_auth_register.s3_do: Set up your profile if you want
education_auth_register.why: rights here are inherent — the app never grants them, it only recognises them once you live somewhere. Registering is bookkeeping, not permission.
education_civic_commons_halls.learn: Live discussion tied to government business — and you can turn something said here into sealed testimony.
education_civic_commons_halls.s1_detail: Same binding to bills, referendums and committees as the threaded halls.
education_civic_commons_halls.s2_detail: A spoken or typed contribution becomes part of the permanent record when you file it.
education_civic_commons_halls.s2_do: Seal a live message as testimony
education_civic_commons_halls.why: nothing is on the record until someone deliberately puts it there. Live talk is talk; testimony is a filing.
education_civic_commons_square.learn: The live, real-time version of the square, carried over the mesh so people on different servers share one room.
education_civic_commons_square.s1_detail: Real-time chat and voice, as opposed to the threaded square.
education_civic_commons_square.s2_detail: The live room is residency-only; the threaded square is open to anyone signed in. Same principle, different rooms.
education_civic_commons_square.s2_do: Note the difference from the threaded square
education_civic_commons_square.why: the permanent record and the live conversation are different things with different rules. The record is uncensorable and open; the live room is a place your neighbours hold.
education_civic_halls.learn: Where discussion attaches to actual government business — a bill, a referendum, a petition, a committee — and where you can put testimony permanently on the record.
education_civic_halls.s1_detail: Halls bind themselves to real governance objects, so the conversation sits with the decision.
education_civic_halls.s1_do: Find the hall for the thing you care about
education_civic_halls.s2_detail: Same open posting as the square.
education_civic_halls.s3_detail: This is the step that differs: sealing puts your words into the permanent public record, and it requires residency in that jurisdiction.
education_civic_halls.why: talking is open to everyone; testifying to a government is an act of a person that government answers to. That is the one place residency matters here — and it is about the record, not about who may speak.
education_civic_home.learn: Your civic front page: what is happening where you live, and what is yours to act on right now.
education_civic_home.s1_detail: You belong to every jurisdiction that contains you — neighbourhood up to the planet — and each one may have its own business.
education_civic_home.s1_do: Read what is live in your places
education_civic_home.s2_detail: Ballots, petitions, and meetings you can join appear here. Anything you cannot act on yet says plainly why.
education_civic_home.s2_do: Act on what is open to you
education_civic_home.s3_detail: It tells you whether residency is confirmed. If it is, you can vote and stand for office — there is no other requirement.
education_civic_home.why: one person is a resident of many nested places at once, and each of those places governs itself. This screen is the join of all of them.
education_civic_identity_verification.le: Optional. It exists for situations that need a verified identity — and it is never a requirement for voting or for standing for office.
education_civic_identity_verification.s1: Nothing on this screen is required to participate in governance.
Submit verification only if you want or need it
education_civic_identity_verification.s2: It does not speed up residency, does not grant a role, and does not unlock a right you did not already have.
Understand what it does not do
education_civic_identity_verification.wh: the app's validator carries a hard list of things that may never be attached to a rights-bearing form — including requires_identity_verification. A filing that tried to make identity a condition of voting would be rejected by the engine, not merely discouraged.
education_civic_journey.s1_detail: Each step names the real form or process behind it, so you can go and find it.
education_civic_journey.s2_detail: Self-reported by design — nothing is checking up on you.
education_civic_journey.s2_do: Tick it off when you understand it
education_civic_journey.s3_detail: The achievement lands on your record and freezes. An achievement never changes a vote, a seat, or what you are allowed to do.
education_civic_journeys.learn: Guided walkthroughs of how the world actually works — an election end to end, a bill becoming law, a court case from filing to opinion.
education_civic_journeys.s1_detail: Each one is a real process in this app, broken into its actual steps.
education_civic_journeys.s2_detail: These are a tour you tick off yourself, not a record of what you did. They are here to explain, not to certify.
education_civic_journeys.s3_detail: Completing the arc records an achievement. It grants nothing — not a vote, not a seat, not a capability.
education_civic_journeys.why: the app is a lot of machinery. Journeys are the map. They deliberately give you nothing, so that learning your way around can never become a requirement for participating.
education_civic_live_room.learn: Every meeting in this world — committee, chamber, an executive's table, courtroom, board, forum, town hall, or a circle of friends — is one room you can walk into. For public bodies the gallery is always open, resident or not; private groups set their own door.
education_civic_live_room.s1_detail: Sessions, committees, courts, and referendum town halls are public to watch for anyone — you never need residency just to see government work. Organization and group rooms decide their own visibility; that freedom is theirs.
education_civic_live_room.s2_detail: In a governed body the first two slots are locked by constitutional order — outstanding emergency powers first, constitutional matters second — and the chair orders the rest. A group of friends has no such lock; its own rules of order apply.
education_civic_live_room.s3_detail: Residents raise a hand for the floor; the chair recognizes speakers and runs the clock. Chat runs under your pseudonymous handle, never a legal name — and in the halls you may file your own message as testimony, sealed to the permanent public record.
education_civic_live_room.s3_do: Speak — and seal it if you mean it
education_civic_live_room.s4_detail: When the chair calls the question, both bars count every serving seat — quorum is a majority of ALL serving, so an absent member counts the same as a no and the bar never shrinks when people stay home. The page never does its own math; the numbers come from the counting engine.
education_civic_live_room.why: This room cannot be censored. No operator, legislator, or judge may remove a post for its viewpoint — the only removals are four narrow carve-outs (a judicial order, protecting another's rights, your own block, content-neutral anti-spam), and every removal is itself a public record.
education_civic_my_record.learn: Everything the app holds about you, in one place — what is public, what is private, and what you can change.
education_civic_my_record.s1_detail: Your acts as an officeholder or candidate are public by constitutional design. Your ordinary life here is not.
education_civic_my_record.s2_detail: Your profile is self-managed. You never file a request to change your own details.
education_civic_my_record.s2_do: Edit what is yours to edit
education_civic_my_record.s3_detail: They record what you have done. An achievement never changes a vote, a seat, or what you are allowed to do — and they are private unless you choose to show them.
education_civic_my_record.why: the line is drawn at power. Hold power and the record is public, permanently. Live your life and it is yours.
education_civic_petition_detail.learn: One petition, its text, its signatures, and exactly where it stands.
education_civic_petition_detail.s1_detai: What you sign is what goes forward — the wording does not change underneath you.
education_civic_petition_detail.s1_do: Read the full text before signing
education_civic_petition_detail.s2_detai: You can change your mind — right up until the audited count freezes.
education_civic_petition_detail.s2_do: Sign, or withdraw a signature you already gave
education_civic_petition_detail.s3_detai: The election board audits the signatures; a court can review the petition's constitutionality before it proceeds.
education_civic_petition_detail.why: a signature is revocable because consent that cannot be withdrawn is not consent. It stops being revocable at the audit, because a count has to be a count.
education_civic_petitions.learn: How people make law without waiting for a legislature to agree.
education_civic_petitions.s1_detail: Anyone associated with the jurisdiction can sign.
education_civic_petitions.s1_do: Read the open petitions where you live
education_civic_petitions.s2_detail: Your signature is a civic act on the record.
education_civic_petitions.s3_detail: You write the text. If it reaches the signature threshold, the legislature must take it up.
education_civic_petitions.why: Art. II §6 is the escape hatch from a legislature that will not act. The threshold is a percentage of the jurisdiction's population, so a small place needs few signatures and a large one needs many — the bar scales with who has to be persuaded.
education_civic_public_square.learn: The open public forum for your jurisdiction. It cannot be censored — and that is a constitutional rule, not a policy the operators chose.
education_civic_public_square.s1_detail: Anyone signed in can post here — resident or not. The square is open; residency gates powers, never speech.
education_civic_public_square.s2_detail: Blocking is your private act. It changes your view and nobody else's.
education_civic_public_square.s2_do: Block anyone you do not want to hear
education_civic_public_square.s3_detail: A post can be removed only by judicial order, to protect someone else's rights, by your own block, or by content-neutral anti-spam. Every removal is logged with its reason.
education_civic_public_square.why: there is no "violates our guidelines" here, and no operator or legislature can add one. The removal check accepts exactly two reasons and demands a reference for each — a takedown on any other ground is refused by the engine.
education_civic_relocation.learn: What happens to your civic life when you move.
education_civic_relocation.s1_detail: You do not file a transfer. Association follows where you actually are.
education_civic_relocation.s2_detail: Sustained residence in the new place confirms there, and the old association lapses on its own.
education_civic_relocation.s3_detail: Your history stays with you. What changes is where you vote, not who you are.
education_civic_relocation.why: the franchise follows the person, automatically. Nobody can strand you between two places, and nobody has to approve your move.
education_civic_residency.learn: This is the one screen that matters most. Confirming where you live is the only thing standing between you and the right to vote and to run for office.
education_civic_residency.s1_detail: You name the place. Nobody approves it — you are not asking permission.
education_civic_residency.s2_detail: Your device checks in quietly in the background. The pings prove presence; they are private and are never published.
education_civic_residency.s2_do: Let the app confirm you are there over time
education_civic_residency.s3_detail: The system files the confirmation itself once you have been there long enough. You do not have to ask, and no official signs off.
education_civic_residency.s4_detail: The moment residency is confirmed you are Associated, and Voter is emitted in the same breath. There is no separate approval, no waiting list, no test.
education_civic_residency.s4_do: Your rights switch on — all of them, at once
education_civic_residency.why: Art. I says you may vote "regardless of any characteristic except jurisdictional association." The code takes that literally — Voter (R-04) is derived identically to Associated (R-03), so nothing can ever be inserted between living somewhere and voting there.
education_civic_rooms.learn: Your direct and group messages live here — private conversations for talk, files, voice, and video. This is the private half of your civic life: only the people in a conversation can read it.
education_civic_rooms.s1_detail: A conversation is gated by membership and nothing else — no office, no role, no residency lets anyone else in. If you are not in it, you never see it, and there is no directory of rooms to browse.
education_civic_rooms.s1_do: Open a conversation from the inbox
education_civic_rooms.s2_detail: One person makes a direct message; a few make a group message. Either way it is just people talking — nothing is filed, and nothing enters the public record.
education_civic_rooms.s3_detail: Text, files, voice, and video share one toolkit, the same for two people or ten. A live group can open a voice and video room in one tap.
education_civic_rooms.s3_do: Say it however it needs saying
education_civic_rooms.s4_detail: A post in the public square is on the record and open to anyone signed in. A message here is private like a ballot. The same Article that keeps the square open keeps this room closed.
education_civic_rooms.s4_do: Know which half you are standing in
education_dev_electoral_kit.learn: Development harness. Not product UI — excluded from the education pass.
education_dev_executive_kit.learn: Development harness. Not product UI — excluded from the education pass.
education_dev_judiciary_kit.learn: Development harness. Not product UI — excluded from the education pass.
education_dev_legislature_kit.learn: A development harness for checking components against fixtures. Not product UI — it is not part of anyone's civic life and carries no education content.
education_economy_agreement_detail.learn: One agreement, in full: its parties, its terms, where it stands. You are reading it because you are named in it — nobody else can.
education_economy_agreement_detail.s1_de: Each party appears in their own role, identified by the residency-confirmed record — never by a paid account or a verification tier. The terms are private to the people named here.
education_economy_agreement_detail.s1_do: Read the terms and the parties
education_economy_agreement_detail.s2_de: Your decision is recorded against your own identity only. Signing binds you once everyone has signed; declining means the agreement simply never exists. The absence of one signature is the absence of the agreement.
education_economy_agreement_detail.s3_de: No clause here can waive a right — an offending clause is void while the rest stands — and work terms can never sign away the workers' right to board representation.
education_economy_agreement_detail.s4_de: Once every party has signed, the contract adds one worker to the organization's headcount. That count — computed from the contracts, never declared by the owners — is what earns workers their first board seat at 100 and equal seats at 2,000.
education_economy_agreement_detail.s4_do: If it is recurring work, know what signing sets in motion
education_economy_agreements.learn: Any two or more parties may freely set terms between themselves — that is the freedom to contract. But every agreement sits on a floor: no clause may waive, sell, or sign away a constitutional right, and nothing binds until every party signs.
education_economy_agreements.s1_detail: Recurring work, an ownership transfer, a sale, a shared account, or anything custom — each kind files as its own record. A recurring work agreement also registers you as a worker of that organization.
education_economy_agreements.s2_detail: A one-sided contract never takes effect. Until each named party has signed, the agreement does not exist and binds no one — there is no provisional or default-on state.
education_economy_agreements.s3_detail: A clause that touches voting, candidacy, residency, petitioning, or due process is void — the rest of the agreement stands. And no agreement may put a price on exercising a civic right.
education_economy_agreements.s4_detail: An agreement's terms are readable only by its parties, like a ballot. What becomes public is only what the agreement causes — a worker headcount, a movement between accounts — never the terms themselves.
education_economy_agreements.why: Both-must-sign is not a policy the app checks — it is a rule the data store itself enforces. The record physically cannot be marked in force until every named party's signature timestamp exists, so no bug, admin, or clever code path can ever activate a one-sided contract.
education_economy_exchange.learn: The trading floor for organization shares — a live tape, an order book, and the recent trades, all in the open. Single items sell on the open market; only shares trade here.
education_economy_exchange.s1_detail: Tapping brings that share into focus: last price, change, volume, and its recent trend. A CGC tag means a common-good corporation quoting on identical terms — its work stays public domain forever.
education_economy_exchange.s1_do: Watch the tape, tap a symbol
education_economy_exchange.s2_detail: Bids are what buyers will pay; asks are what sellers want; the gap between them is the spread. Price discovery happens in the open — everyone sees the same book.
education_economy_exchange.s3_detail: A matched order forms an agreement between the two parties and settles to their private wallets. No payment rails, no custody, no shared pot — the floor discovers the price, the parties own the trade.
education_economy_exchange.s3_do: Understand what a matched trade becomes
education_economy_exchange.s4_detail: Single items sell at one place and one price on the open market — this floor is only for shares.
education_economy_exchange.s4_do: Buy goods on the open market instead
education_economy_home.learn: Everything you trade, agree, earn, and owe — in one place. The unit you see on every price is an abstract unit of account: it counts value inside the game and never touches outside money — no payment rails, no custody.
education_economy_home.s1_detail: The cards route you to the open market, the exchange, agreements, your wallet, joint ledgers, units & money, the civic stipend, public finance, and org economics. The square is for talk; the market is for trade.
education_economy_home.s2_detail: The recurring economy run fires on an interval set by law — changing the cycle takes the same two doors as any money rule. It is a law, not an admin knob.
education_economy_home.s3_detail: Your economic data is private to you, the way a ballot is. The currency is reserved to the most-encompassing jurisdiction. And money rules move only through two doors — a supermajority of the chamber and the consent of the people it governs.
education_economy_home.s3_do: Read the rails that hold everywhere
education_economy_home.why: No paywall on civic rights. No tax, fee, or cost may ever attach to voting, candidacy, residency, or petitioning — you can go broke here and lose nothing that matters. Wealth buys goods; it never buys governance. (Art. I)
education_economy_joint_ledgers.learn: A joint ledger is a co-owned account: its balance belongs to more than one party, and no movement leaves it until every required co-owner agrees. One signer can never move shared money alone.
education_economy_joint_ledgers.s1_detai: Every ledger names its co-owners and its approval rule up front — all signers, or a majority, as agreed when it opened. Every co-owner must accept before the ledger exists at all.
education_economy_joint_ledgers.s1_do: Read the rule before the balance
education_economy_joint_ledgers.s2_detai: Any co-owner can propose a payment, a transfer, a drawdown. The parties set their own rule and purpose freely — but no clause in the agreement may waive a constitutional right.
education_economy_joint_ledgers.s3_detai: Your signature is one of several. The movement waits, showing who has agreed and who is still needed, and settles only when the rule is met.
education_economy_joint_ledgers.s4_detai: A jurisdiction-owned shared fund posts to the public record, where every entry is chained to the one before so history cannot be quietly rewritten. A ledger between people or organizations is readable only by its co-owners.
education_economy_listing_detail.learn: One offer, end to end — what it is, who is selling it, and exactly what happens when you order. Your receipt is private: like a ballot, only buyer and seller can read it.
education_economy_listing_detail.s1_deta: The price, the quantity, the seller and what kind of seller they are. A Common Good Corp badge means identical terms to any private seller — and work that stays public domain forever.
education_economy_listing_detail.s1_do: Read the listing like the contract offer it is
education_economy_listing_detail.s2_deta: Your order files against the listing. You are committing to buy at the listed price; nothing binds until the seller accepts.
education_economy_listing_detail.s3_deta: Only the seller settles an order — a buyer can never complete their own purchase. On acceptance the order becomes a two-sided agreement, and no clause in it may waive a right.
education_economy_listing_detail.s3_do: Wait for the seller to accept
education_economy_listing_detail.s4_deta: The units move account to account — a debit to yours, a credit to the seller's. No payment rail, no middleman, and nobody else can read the movement.
education_economy_marketplace.learn: One market, two directions: offers are what people will give, requests are what people need. It is open to every resident — no licence, no membership, no permission needed, and the app deliberately checks for none.
education_economy_marketplace.s1_detail: Offers are goods and services for sale. Requests are work postings and neighbors asking for a hand. Same market, opposite directions.
education_economy_marketplace.s1_do: Browse offers, or switch to requests
education_economy_marketplace.s2_detail: One form puts a good or a service on the market. A person, a business, a nonprofit, and a common-good corporation all list on identical terms — nobody gets a better counter.
education_economy_marketplace.s3_detail: Ordering opens a purchase against the seller's listing. Nothing binds until the seller accepts — a one-sided contract never takes effect.
education_economy_marketplace.s3_do: Place an order on an offer
education_economy_marketplace.s4_detail: No price, no contract — a neighbor asking for help is not a trade, so the app puts no market machinery on it. Private by default — it is shared only as far as the asker chooses.
education_economy_marketplace.s4_do: Ask or answer under mutual aid
education_economy_org_settings.learn: The steward's view of an organization's economic life — its board split, shares, dues, ledger, and taxes — each fenced by a floor no charter or rule-change can cross. Most players never need this page.
education_economy_org_settings.s1_detail: The worker/owner split is computed from the labor agreements on record, never negotiated or declared: the first worker seat arrives at 100 workers, parity at 2,000. One hire can change the board.
education_economy_org_settings.s1_do: Review the board and worker seats
education_economy_org_settings.s2_detail: Stock-held organizations list their share classes and holders; equal-partnership and member-owned organizations carry no shares at all — ownership follows the charter. An ownership stake moves only by a transfer both sides sign. A common-good corporation's intellectual property stays public domain forever.
education_economy_org_settings.s3_detail: Dues are a voluntary agreement between a member and an organization that chooses to charge them. Let them lapse and the membership ends — nothing else does. No due, fee, or cost may ever gate a civic right.
education_economy_org_settings.s4_detail: The organization's own ledger — balances, receipts, movements — is private to the organization, like a ballot. The levies it owes are apportioned from the population records, never assessed against anyone's civic rights.
education_economy_org_settings.s4_do: Know what stays private and what is apportioned
education_economy_request_detail.learn: One job on the board, end to end: the rate, the organization, and what an accepted application sets in motion — down to the board seat it can help earn.
education_economy_request_detail.s1_deta: Any resident may apply — there is no means test and no qualification gate, and applying never touches a civic right. Your application is visible only to you and the organization.
education_economy_request_detail.s2_deta: Acceptance is the trigger. Nothing binds until both sides act — a one-sided contract never takes effect.
education_economy_request_detail.s3_deta: On acceptance, you file the worker registration — the record is yours, not the employer's. It captures the recurring work agreement both of you sign.
education_economy_request_detail.s3_do: Your work agreement goes on the record
education_economy_request_detail.s4_deta: The new contract raises the organization's worker headcount. At 100 workers the board gains its first worker seat; at 2,000, workers and owners hold equal board power.
education_economy_request_detail.why: The headcount math is hardened — no labor contract can bargain away representation. The hire that crosses 100 changes the boardroom, and no clause the employer writes can undo it. (Art. III §6)
education_economy_stipend.learn: Every resident receives the civic stipend — a shared floor, plus a small capped bump for people carrying certain duties. It is a differential, not a salary: it grants no seat, no vote, no advantage of any kind.
education_economy_stipend.s1_detail: The only gate is an active residency, the same absolute gate as voting. There is no means test, no application, no age line, no good-standing check — and none can ever be added.
education_economy_stipend.s1_do: Confirm residency — that is the whole test
education_economy_stipend.s2_detail: Your amount is the floor plus the sum of your duty bumps, capped. A bump attaches to a fact about what you are doing — running a node, moderating, holding office — and it ends the day the duty ends. Stacking can never exceed the cap.
education_economy_stipend.s3_detail: Each run posts one public line: the total paid and a head-count. Your own amount writes only to your private wallet, and any bump class small enough that a published total would give someone's amount away is folded into the general figure instead.
education_economy_stipend.s3_do: Check the public total against your private receipt
education_economy_stipend.s4_detail: The floor, the cap, and every bump move only by a two-door act — chamber supermajority plus constituent consent. Zeroing the stipend changes nobody's eligibility for anything.
education_economy_stipend.s4_do: Propose a change through the chamber
education_economy_stipend.why: If a treasury-funded run cannot cover everyone, the system short-pays everyone by the same fraction and says so publicly. Paying the first names on the list and stopping would draw an arbitrary line between people the constitution treats identically — so the code refuses to be able to.
education_economy_treasury.learn: How your jurisdiction raises, budgets, and spends money — entirely in the open. Public money is public record: anyone may read this page, resident or not, because a ledger you cannot inspect is not a public ledger.
education_economy_treasury.s1_detail: The legislature enacts the budget as an ordinary act, and enactment itself spawns the spending authority for each line — a budget and its appropriations are born together, never one without the other.
education_economy_treasury.s2_detail: Every row is double-entry: it names where value left and where it landed, so the books always balance — except issuance, the one lawful entry where money comes into existence at the root (Art. V §5) with no source to name. Rows are append-only and hash-chained — each row carries the fingerprint of the one before it, so nothing is ever edited or deleted without breaking the chain; a correction is a new balancing entry with its own line in history.
education_economy_treasury.s3_detail: Jurisdiction and department accounts are public — balance and every movement. Individual and organization accounts are private, readable only by their owner, like a ballot. Transfers name accounts, never people.
education_economy_treasury.s3_do: Tell public accounts from private ones
education_economy_treasury.s4_detail: Levies and borrowing happen only by act — the executive disburses what was appropriated and authorizes nothing. And no tax, fee, or cost may ever attach to voting, candidacy, residency, or petitioning.
education_economy_treasury.s4_do: Know what only the legislature can do
education_economy_treasury.why: Exactly one piece of code in the entire system can move value, and the test suite scans the source to keep it that way. With one writer and no side door, "the books balance" is a property of the system itself — not a report somebody has to run and everybody has to trust.
education_economy_units.learn: This is the money itself — the unit of account, what it is worth, how it subdivides — and every lever that sets those things. No lever here is an admin knob: each one moves only by a legislative act, and the currency is produced by the most-encompassing jurisdiction alone.
education_economy_units.s1_detail: Name, symbol, precision, and the stack of subdivisions. Defining the unit and its subdivisions is the power to set measurement standards — one shared yardstick for the whole federation, so it lives at the root, and no lower jurisdiction may mint.
education_economy_units.s2_detail: Every value shown — issuance rate, inflation target, the stipend dials — was set by a legislative act and carries the act that set it. There is no settings screen behind this page; the only write path is a bill.
education_economy_units.s3_detail: A monetary lever moves only when two doors open: a supermajority of the chamber, and then the consent of the constituent jurisdictions whose money it is. Where a jurisdiction has no constituents, the second door is satisfied by itself — but it is never skipped where they exist.
education_economy_units.s4_detail: How often the economy pays out is itself one of the settings, changed by the same two-door act as every other lever. Nothing about the money's rhythm belongs to an operator.
education_economy_units.s4_do: Notice the clock is a lever too
education_economy_units.why: The demo runs a social-credit unit, but nothing here depends on that. The constitution fixes who decides and how — never which currency. The machinery takes no position on how much money should exist; that question belongs entirely to the people whose money it is.
education_economy_wallet.learn: Your balance and every receipt, private the way a ballot is private — only you can read them. Nothing here holds or moves real money; the unit is an abstract measure of value inside the game.
education_economy_wallet.s1_detail: Credits in, debits out, each with its counterpart account and memo. This list is yours alone — it is never published, shared, or federated.
education_economy_wallet.s2_detail: The civic stipend is always on, for everyone — a floor everyone shares plus a small bump for civic work, under a cap. It can only credit you, never withhold, and its size changes no eligibility for anything.
education_economy_wallet.s3_detail: A transfer names the recipient's account, never a person. Your own account is resolved from your identity, and the form can never be used to discover who owns an account. An overdraft is refused; so is paying yourself.
education_economy_wallet.s3_do: Send a transfer — to an account
education_economy_wallet.why: Transfers address accounts because ledgers record value, not identity. If transfers took names, every ledger would slowly become a map of people — addressing accounts keeps who-you-are permanently separate from what-you-hold, the same separation a ballot enjoys.
education_elections_board_console.learn: The working surface for the people who run an election — and the limits on what they can touch.
education_elections_board_console.s1_det: Scheduling and validation are the board's core acts.
education_elections_board_console.s1_do: Call the election and validate candidacies
education_elections_board_console.s2_det: Boundaries are versioned; old plans are archived, never overwritten.
education_elections_board_console.s3_det: Certification seats the winners automatically. Audits and recounts are filed acts on the public record.
education_elections_board_console.why: a board runs the process and cannot touch the count. The finalist number is pre-published, the counting method is hardened in code, and certification is the trigger for seating rather than a decision about who won.
education_elections_candidacy_registrati: How you put your name forward. There is nothing to qualify for.
If you are associated with the jurisdiction, you may stand. No fee, no signatures, no endorsement, no approval.
The board checks one thing: that you are actually associated here. It is a check, not a judgement.

Art. I gives the right to stand for office "regardless of any characteristic except jurisdictional association." The validator refuses any filing that tries to attach a fee or an eligibility condition to this form — the app will not let a legislature invent one.
education_elections_candidate_profile.le: What a candidate says for themselves, and who has backed them.
education_elections_candidate_profile.s1: Candidate platforms are mandatory-public — standing for power means saying what you would do with it.
education_elections_candidate_profile.s2: You request; the organisation decides. Its grant is always public.
Ask an organisation to endorse you
education_elections_candidate_profile.s3: Standing down is your own act.
Withdraw if you change your mind
education_elections_candidate_profile.wh: endorsements inform, they never gate. A candidate with no endorsements appears on the ballot exactly like any other — running unendorsed is first-class. Any organisation or individual can be an endorser on the record; there is no party layer and no slate.
education_elections_detail.learn: One election end to end: when it was called, who is standing, how it will be counted, and when each stage closes.
education_elections_detail.s1_detail: Every deadline is published with the order that called the election, not decided as it goes.
education_elections_detail.s2_detail: How many candidates advance is fixed and published up front, derived from the number of seats. Nobody adjusts it once they can see who is winning.
education_elections_detail.s3_detail: The board certifies the result; a recount or audit can be ordered on the record.
education_elections_open_ballot.learn: The first round. Everyone standing appears; you mark everyone you would be content with.
education_elections_open_ballot.s1_detai: This is not a choice of one. Approve everybody you could live with.
education_elections_open_ballot.s1_do: Approve as many as you like
education_elections_open_ballot.s2_detai: The filter offers organisations, "individual endorsers", or "no endorsements". There is no party column, because there are no parties in the model.
education_elections_open_ballot.s2_do: Filter by who has endorsed them, if it helps
education_elections_open_ballot.s3_detai: Approval picks the finalists. It does not pick the winners.
education_elections_ranked_ballot.learn: The round that fills the seats. You rank the finalists; the count does the rest.
education_elections_ranked_ballot.s1_det: Ranking your real favourite first can never hurt them. There is no tactical reason to rank dishonestly.
education_elections_ranked_ballot.s1_do: Rank the finalists in your true order
education_elections_ranked_ballot.s2_det: Your ballot is separated from your identity at the moment it is cast.
education_elections_ranked_ballot.s3_det: You can check your ballot was included, without revealing what it said.
education_elections_ranked_ballot.why: seats are filled by single transferable vote with a Droop quota. A vote for someone who has already won, or who cannot win, transfers instead of being thrown away — which is why almost no vote is wasted and why the chamber ends up proportional without anyone sorting people into blocs.
education_elections_results.learn: The count, round by round, and how to check it yourself.
education_elections_results.s1_detail: Every transfer and elimination is shown. The count is not a black box that emits a winner.
education_elections_results.s2_detail: Check your receipt against the published set.
education_elections_results.s3_detail: Observation and audit standing belongs to the endorsing organisations and the candidates themselves.
education_elections_vacancy_countback.le: What happens when a seat empties mid-term — and why there is usually no by-election.
education_elections_vacancy_countback.s1: A vacancy is declared on the record before anything else happens.
education_elections_vacancy_countback.s2: The original ballots are re-run with the departed member removed as a candidate. Every prior ballot counts, with no filtering anywhere in the procedure.
education_elections_vacancy_countback.s3: If the countback cannot fill the seat, a special election runs within 90–180 days.
education_elections_vacancy_countback.wh: the people who elected that chamber already expressed a full ranking. Asking them again would let a different, smaller electorate decide — so the app asks their original ballots instead. That is what "universal" countback means.
education_executive_department_detail.le: One department: its mandate, its governors, its rules and its reports.
education_executive_department_detail.s1: A department can only act inside the scope its creating act gave it.
education_executive_department_detail.s2: Ten years, in lockstep with judicial appointments — long enough to outlast the politics.
See the governors and their terms
education_executive_department_detail.s3: Rules are filed acts, on the record.
Read the rules it has implemented
education_executive_department_reporting: What departments must publish about themselves, and when.
Reporting is a constitutional obligation, not a courtesy.
Transparency is the mechanism that makes a ten-year term safe.
education_executive_departments.learn: The standing offices that actually do the work — and how each one came to exist.
education_executive_departments.s1_detai: Each was created by an act of the legislature, not by executive fiat.
education_executive_departments.s2_detai: Departments are run by a Board of Governors, seated on ten-year terms.
education_executive_executive_actions.le: Orders and decisions the executive has issued — and the check that runs before any of them can be.
education_executive_executive_actions.s1: Every executive order is a public act from the moment it is issued.
education_executive_executive_actions.s2: Scope is validated before an order can issue. An order outside the executive's delegated authority is refused by the engine, not litigated afterwards.
education_executive_executive_actions.s3: Departmental investigations and Board of Governors nominations are filed acts too.
education_executive_executive_actions.wh: the dangerous executive act is the one nobody sees until it has already happened. Validating scope before issuance is what stops the order existing in the first place.
education_executive_executive_home.learn: The doing arm of a government: who carries out the laws, and who they answer to.
education_executive_executive_home.s1_de: An executive starts as something the legislature delegates, not as a separate throne.
education_executive_executive_home.s2_de: Either a committee of five or more with equal voting power, or a single officeholder with the top four runners-up seated automatically as advisors.
education_executive_executive_home.s3_de: It executes the laws; the legislature that created it can convert, constrain or remove it.
education_executive_executive_home.why: the executive is the only branch that begins as a loan of someone else's power. Becoming directly elected takes a supermajority and the constituents' agreement.
education_groups_create.learn: Start a conversation — one person for a direct message, a few for a group. There is no registration and no filing: a group here is informal by design.
education_groups_create.s1_detail: You choose who is in — that choice is the only membership rule there is. Nobody approves the group, and nobody outside it can read it.
education_groups_create.s1_do: Add the people it is with
education_groups_create.s2_detail: The name is for the people in it. It appears in no register and no public list — an unnamed group is exactly as real as a named one.
education_groups_create.s2_do: Name it if you want to
education_groups_create.s3_detail: Nothing files anywhere when you press start. The absence of a form is the point: your private associations are not the government's to record.
education_groups_create.s4_detail: A group that finds a lasting purpose can register as an organization and gain a public home, durable membership, and elections of its own. That step is always the group's choice, never a requirement.
education_groups_create.s4_do: Let it outgrow itself — if it ever wants to
education_groups_detail.learn: One conversation: the messages, the people in it, and a live voice and video room one tap away. The group decides its own visibility — nobody outside it can look in.
education_groups_detail.s1_detail: Messages, files, voice, and video all live in the one thread. None of it is testimony and none of it is on the record — this is conversation, not governance.
education_groups_detail.s1_do: Talk, and attach what the talk needs
education_groups_detail.s2_detail: A group conversation carries its own voice and video room. It is the group's room: joining needs an invitation to the group, nothing more and nothing less.
education_groups_detail.s3_detail: Anyone in the group can bring someone in, and anyone can walk out. No exit process, no approval. When the last person leaves, the conversation is gone.
education_groups_detail.s3_do: Add people, or leave — freely, at any time
education_groups_detail.s4_detail: The group can register as an organization to gain a public page and lasting membership. Registered or not, it holds no governance power; until it registers it appears on no public surface — both by design.
education_groups_detail.s4_do: Make it a standing organization — only if it wants one
education_invite_landing.learn: This is how most people arrive — a friend's link. An invite is a doorway and nothing more: it shows you honestly where it leads, asks at most what to call you, and grants no power to anyone on either side of it.
education_invite_landing.s1_detail: You see a truthful preview of the destination — the real room, who's inside, whether it's live now. An expired or invalid link still opens the front door; it never dead-ends you.
education_invite_landing.s2_detail: Public rooms are open to watch without an account — no email, no ID, nothing to fill in. When you want a voice — to speak on the record, vote, or stand for office — you create an account and say where you live. Living somewhere is the only requirement there is.
education_invite_landing.s3_detail: If you do sign in, the app remembers the destination and carries you there afterward. The link's secret is proven once at the door and never stored.
education_invite_landing.why: An invite carries attribution, never privilege. Nobody gains a vote, a seat, or an advantage by inviting you — the growth of this world is deliberately disconnected from power inside it, so bringing friends can never become a way to accumulate anything but company.
education_judiciary_advocate_console.lea: The working surface for advocates — the people who argue cases for others.
education_judiciary_advocate_console.s1_: Registration confers R-21. The bar is open to residents.
education_judiciary_advocate_console.s2_: Case filings, motions, evidence and briefs on behalf of a client.
education_judiciary_case_detail.learn: One case from filing to judgment — panel, evidence, jury, ruling.
education_judiciary_case_detail.s1_detai: Judges are assigned to a panel; jurors are summoned by order.
education_judiciary_case_detail.s1_do: Follow the panel and the jury
education_judiciary_case_detail.s2_detai: Motions, evidence and arguments are on the record as they are submitted.
education_judiciary_case_detail.s3_detai: Opinions, sentences and warrants are all published acts.
education_judiciary_case_detail.why: you cannot be tried twice for the same thing. Double jeopardy is enforced by the engine, not by a judge remembering.
education_judiciary_case_docket.learn: Every case before this court, and how a case gets in.
education_judiciary_case_docket.s2_detai: You can file yourself, or an advocate can file for you.
education_judiciary_case_docket.s3_detai: The court classifies justiciability and severity at acceptance and assigns a panel.
education_judiciary_constitutional_chall: How anyone can challenge a law — and the one place in the app where a court can change the law directly.
Any inhabitant may file. There is no standing gatekeeper, no fee, and no eligibility test beyond living here.
The court makes a constitutional finding and may recommend a remedy.
Where the path allows it, the court edits the law itself — and the full version history is preserved.
A chamber can override a judicial outcome by the constitutional route, not by ignoring it.
this is the deepest act in the app. It is deliberately open to anyone who lives there, because a constitution that only lawyers can invoke belongs to lawyers.
education_judiciary_judiciary_home.learn: The courts for this jurisdiction: how they were created, who sits on them, and how they are chosen.
education_judiciary_judiciary_home.s1_de: A legislature creates it by supermajority act.
education_judiciary_judiciary_home.s2_de: Appointed by default, for ten-year terms. Nominations are consented to by the chamber.
education_judiciary_judiciary_home.s3_de: A judiciary can be made elected instead — but that takes a supermajority and the constituents' agreement.
education_judiciary_judiciary_home.why: appointment is the default because a judge who must campaign has an incentive to please. Ten-year terms and a hard floor of five judges per court are there for the same reason.
education_judiciary_juror_view.learn: What you see if you are summoned, and what is expected of you.
education_judiciary_juror_view.s1_detail: It names the order that created it.
education_judiciary_juror_view.s2_detail: Jurors file nothing. Your role is to hear and decide, not to submit forms.
education_jurisdictions_bootstrap.learn: Every place on the map starts dormant — its boundary already loaded, waiting for residents. Governing begins wherever enough verified people actually live: a county can wake before its state, and the first election fires itself the moment the threshold is crossed.
education_jurisdictions_bootstrap.s1_det: The count is verified residencies, not raw signups — every confirmation the system files adds one to the live census, and the threshold itself is amendable per jurisdiction tier.
education_jurisdictions_bootstrap.s2_det: Until a legislature exists, the system itself acts as the election board using the constitution's defaults: the standard proportional ranked vote, 5-year terms, districts of 5–9 seats. Nobody has to ask for this election; it is triggered, not requested.
education_jurisdictions_bootstrap.s2_do: Cross the threshold — the first election schedules itself
education_jurisdictions_bootstrap.s3_det: Steps run automatically where the constitution allows; elected humans take over from stage 4 — the legislature constitutes, then the executive, then the judiciary, until full governance is achieved.
education_jurisdictions_bootstrap.s3_do: Follow the 30 steps through their seven stages
education_jurisdictions_bootstrap.s4_det: Step 14 creates the proper independent election board and the system-as-board steps down. Bootstrap scaffolding never outlives its purpose.
education_jurisdictions_bootstrap.s4_do: Watch the temporary board retire itself
education_jurisdictions_disintermediatio: A middle layer of government — a state sitting between its counties and the country — can be dissolved so the places inside it answer directly to the level above. Nobody imposes this from outside: every constituent must agree, and the level above must consent.
A legislature adopts the disintermediation vote, which opens a consent process across every constituent chamber and the encompassing legislature.
Unanimity, not a two-thirds vote: each constituent passes its own act, and one holdout stops the dissolution. The level above must also consent.
Reach unanimity — every constituent, plus the level above

The dissolved layer's acts do not vanish — they fold into each former constituent's own law with full version history preserved. Conflicts with existing local law are surfaced and a resolution recorded before anything takes effect, and open legal challenges travel with the merged law.
When dissolution takes effect, each former constituent answers directly to the level above, and every resident's chain of places re-resolves automatically.

The constituents inherit the removed layer's rules — and from that moment the rules are theirs. Each place can amend or repeal them like any law it passed itself. Dissolving a government never dissolves the law people were living under; it hands the pen to the people closest to it.
education_jurisdictions_federation.learn: When two self-governing neighbors disagree about where their shared edge sits, the people who live inside the moving boundary decide — not the legislatures around them. This screen is your window on what happens between governments; the server plumbing behind them lives in the operator area.
education_jurisdictions_federation.s1_de: The proposal is drafted and deliberated in the open, everyone inside the moving boundary votes in a referendum, then the map updates as a new versioned boundary — history preserved.
education_jurisdictions_federation.s1_do: Follow a boundary change through its three steps
education_jurisdictions_federation.s2_de: Passing takes two-thirds of the whole affected population — never just those who happen to vote, and never either whole jurisdiction. The affected area is the electorate and the denominator.
education_jurisdictions_federation.s3_de: Once ratified, every affected resident's home association is re-checked against the new boundary. Rights re-attach automatically on the new side of the line — nobody has to re-register.
education_jurisdictions_federation.s4_de: Different governments can run on different servers that keep each place's records in sync. Public records and achievements travel across that mesh; your ballot contents and private location pings never do, and your lesson progress stays on your own node and never federates — though a training completion you file is a constitutional act and travels like any other public record. Running a server grants zero governance power — the mesh moves records, never authority.
education_jurisdictions_restoration.lear: If a government is overthrown, captured, or destroyed, the constitution does not pause — rebuilding cascades through three tiers until a legitimate government stands again. This page is the standing drill, dormant until evidence says otherwise.
education_jurisdictions_restoration.s1_d: Countermanded, captured or disabled, or destroyed. Detection is evidence-based and confirmed by a judicial finding — no government can ever flip this switch unilaterally.
education_jurisdictions_restoration.s2_d: Tier 1: the constituents jointly elect a new legislature. Tier 2: the level above calls the elections for them. Tier 3: individuals self-organize new jurisdictions from a dormant boundary. Each tier activates only when the one above it cannot act.
education_jurisdictions_restoration.s3_d: Rebuilding elections reuse the first-election machinery — run by the system with the constitution's defaults, exactly like a place waking up for the first time.
education_jurisdictions_restoration.s4_d: Fewest people governed without consent, no constituency privileged over another, actual ability to govern. Defensive forces are bound to the most legitimate claimant — not the incumbent, not the strongest.
If rivals claim the government, legitimacy is scored
education_jurisdictions_restoration.why: Whatever still functions — elections, sessions, courts — cannot be disrupted while restoration runs, the same hard guarantee that bounds emergency powers. And restoration doubles as a founding path: standing a world up from surviving records is the same act as rebuilding a lost government.
Two or more independent places merge into a union only by their own consent — check where their rules differ, agree one shared value for each difference, then ratify on both sides. There is no live case today (Earth starts united), but the process stands ready for any future independent jurisdictions.

A side-by-side compares each party's settings and institutions. The locked-in mechanics — the voting method, the 5–9 seat range for districts, the two-thirds rule — are identical everywhere by design, so only the amendable values need reconciling.
The founding act records one union value per divergence. Constituents keep their own values for their own scope where the power is joint — joining a union does not flatten local law.
Agree one shared value for each difference

Union formation needs a two-thirds supermajority of individuals in each applicant population and a supermajority of the union's constituent jurisdictions (a founding union has none yet; that meter binds from the first join onward). Denominators are whole populations — never just those who vote.
Leaving runs the same process with the same supermajorities as joining. There are no one-way doors.
Know the door swings both ways

The union is born self-governing with a legislature that seats both kinds of members — seats by population and equal seats per constituent — and both kinds must independently agree for any act to pass. A small partner joins knowing it can never simply be outvoted out of existence.
education_jurisdictions_viewer.learn: One place: its boundaries, its population, its institutions, and whether its government has woken up yet.
education_jurisdictions_viewer.s1_detail: Every jurisdiction sits inside others and may contain others.
education_jurisdictions_viewer.s1_do: See the place and its nesting
education_jurisdictions_viewer.s2_detail: Legislature, executive, judiciary — each present or not.
education_jurisdictions_viewer.s3_detail: A government boots when enough real residents have confirmed there. Until then the scaffolding exists but nothing governs.
education_jurisdictions_viewer.why: every place on Earth exists in the app from the start, but none of them govern until actual people live there and say so. Institutions follow residents, never the other way round.
education_learn_guides.learn: Every how-to on one searchable page — the standard procedure for everything you can do, grouped by the part of the app it belongs to. The manual lives inside the app, not somewhere you have to go find.
education_learn_guides.s1_detail: Type what you are trying to do — matching procedures open in place, and everything else steps aside.
education_learn_guides.s2_detail: Numbered steps, the rule behind each step, the film that shows it, and a way to report a problem right from the panel. Procedures for node operators are labeled, so you always know which ones are about running the system rather than governing with it.
education_learn_guides.s3_detail: If nothing matches, the empty state hands you the report form — a missing guide is a ticket, and filing it is how the next person finds the answer.
education_learn_guides.s3_do: Hit a dead end? Say so
education_learn_home.learn: Every tool comes with a short lesson: a video in your language, the standard procedure, a quick check, and a door straight into the live activity. All of it is open to every user — and none of it is ever a requirement for anything.
education_learn_home.s1_detail: Six tracks run from getting started to running a node, and every lesson stands on its own. There is no prerequisite, no enrollment, and no role you must hold or seek — every training is open to you.
education_learn_home.s2_detail: The bar counts lessons finished. It is for you — finishing lessons grants no vote, no seat, and no capability you didn't already have.
education_learn_home.s3_detail: Finishing files through the constitutional engine like any other civic act and pays the one-time training stipend. Once means once: the achievement ledger remembers each training you've completed, so a retake never pays twice.
education_learn_home.s3_do: Finish a training — it counts once
education_learn_home.s4_detail: The Coalition's free courses cover the principles, the voting math, and the full constitution. Optional, always.
education_learn_home.why: Learning is never a gate. Your right to vote and to stand for office comes from residency alone (Art. I) — no training, test, or certificate can ever be placed in front of it. These lessons exist to make you good at power, not to decide who gets it.
education_learn_lesson.learn: One lesson is a short video, the standard procedure it teaches, a quick check, and a "now do it live" door into the real activity. The check teaches — it never judges, and it never remembers.
education_learn_lesson.s1_detail: The film shows the task in your language; the standard procedure beneath it lists the numbered steps with the rule behind each one.
education_learn_lesson.s2_detail: Pick an answer and read the explanation either way. Your answers are never recorded — not which one you chose, not how many tries it took — and the answer key stays on the server, never sent to your device. Retake as often as you like.
education_learn_lesson.s3_detail: Finishing files a training completion through the constitutional engine, recording one fact only: that you completed. That same filing pays the one-time training stipend — once ever per training, remembered by the achievement ledger.
education_learn_lesson.s4_detail: The door at the bottom drops you into the real journey the lesson taught. That is the point — practice ends here, participation starts there.
education_learn_lesson.why: What files is completion, never answers — the record exists to pay you once and mark the achievement, not to grade you. And completing grants nothing beyond that: no vote, no seat, no standing you didn't already hold from residency alone (Art. I).
A bill here is a conversation you can open while it moves, not a document you find afterward — its progress, its clauses under negotiation, and the public talk around it, all on one page.
Drafted → committee → floor reading → floor vote → law. The stages update as the bill moves, and one click puts you in the gallery of the floor session deciding it.

Proposed changes appear as redlines against specific sections, each with its rationale, so what would change — and why — stays legible to anyone. Comments and redlines are public talk on the bill, kept separate from the formal record that holds the lifecycle and the vote math.
Read the clauses and the redlines
The comment thread is open talk. To put your words on the formal record, file them as testimony in the hall where the bill is heard — sealed permanently under your handle, never your legal name.
Say your piece — twice if you mean it
Once a bill becomes law, any resident may challenge it as unconstitutional. If the judges agree, the remedy can edit the law's text directly — with the full history of every version preserved.
education_legislature_bill_detail.learn: One bill: its text, its committee, its votes, and the exact threshold it must clear.
education_legislature_bill_detail.s1_det: Every version is kept. Nothing is overwritten.
education_legislature_bill_detail.s1_do: Read the text and its history
education_legislature_bill_detail.s2_det: Committee vote first, then the floor.
education_legislature_bill_detail.s2_do: Follow it through committee and floor
education_legislature_bill_detail.s3_det: Ordinary acts need a majority; some need two-thirds of all serving members. The threshold comes from what the act does — it is never chosen by whoever is counting.
education_legislature_bills.learn: Every proposed law in this jurisdiction, and where each one has got to.
education_legislature_bills.s1_detail: Bills are public from introduction, not from passage.
education_legislature_bills.s2_detail: You write it; the chamber decides.
education_legislature_bills.s2_do: Introduce one if you hold a seat
education_legislature_bills.s3_detail: A bill's scale and scope are locked when it is introduced — it cannot quietly grow into something else on the way through.
education_legislature_bills.s3_do: Note what is fixed at introduction
education_legislature_committee_detail.l: One committee at work — meetings, agenda, votes, and the report it sends back.
education_legislature_committee_detail.s: The chair calls the meeting and sets the agenda.
See when it meets and what is on the agenda
Committee members vote here before anything reaches the floor.
A committee refers a bill to the floor and files a report that becomes public record.
education_legislature_committees.learn: How the chamber splits its work up, and how members end up on the committees they are on.
education_legislature_committees.s1_deta: Created by a supermajority act of the chamber.
education_legislature_committees.s1_do: See the committees and who sits on them
education_legislature_committees.s2_deta: You rank them all. You are not assigned by anyone.
education_legislature_committees.s2_do: Rank every committee in your order of preference
education_legislature_committees.s3_deta: Assignment is faction-independent. Placements honour rank order and spread evenly across members — counts differ by at most one. Ties break to the member with the largest vote share after normalising quotas.
education_legislature_committees.why: this is the mechanism that keeps committees proportional without a party layer. Members endorsed by several organisations and members endorsed by none are treated identically — there is no faction to be sorted into.
education_legislature_districts.learn: The map itself — how the seats of a legislature are distributed across real places.
education_legislature_districts.s1_detai: District plans are versioned: adopting a new one archives the old, never overwrites it.
education_legislature_districts.s2_detai: Each district elects between five and nine.
education_legislature_districts.s3_detai: Drawing is a filed act by the election board, on the public record.
education_legislature_districts.why: versioned maps mean a boundary change can always be compared against what it replaced. A redistricting you cannot see the before-and-after of is not reviewable.
education_legislature_emergency_powers.l: The most dangerous power in the constitution, and the three things that box it in.
education_legislature_emergency_powers.s: Active emergency powers are shown on every page of the app, not hidden here.
Disaster or invasion only. The grounds are validated before the vote is taken, not argued about afterwards.
Ninety days, maximum. Renewal is a fresh vote, never automatic, and the ceiling cannot be raised by any act.
A court can review an active declaration.
education_legislature_emergency_powers.w: every historical failure of emergency powers is a failure of the exit, not the entry. So the exit is automatic: the clock runs whether or not anyone remembers to stop it.
education_legislature_index.learn: Every legislature you can see from here, at every level of nesting.
education_legislature_index.s1_detail: A place can have one at every scale — neighbourhood to planet.
education_legislature_index.s2_detail: Districts elect five to nine representatives each. A legislature is composed of districts and scales by the cube root of population — bigger places get more districts, not bigger rooms.
education_legislature_legislature_home.l: The legislature for one place: who holds its seats, what it has adopted, and what it is working on.
education_legislature_legislature_home.s: Seats come from the election, filled proportionally. Members appear with the organisations that endorsed them, if any — running unendorsed is first-class.
Seating is your own act; nobody swears you in.
Take the oath if you were just elected
A chamber adopts its rules of order and ethics code itself.
Legislatures create committees, election boards and administrative offices — the institutions everything else runs on.
education_legislature_legislature_home.w: a legislature is small on purpose. Districts elect five to nine representatives each; a legislature is composed of districts and scales by the cube root of population. Bigger places get more districts, not bigger rooms.
education_legislature_oversight.learn: How a legislature holds officeholders — including its own members — to account.
education_legislature_oversight.s1_detai: Removal, impeachment, censure and expulsion all run through the chamber.
education_legislature_oversight.s2_detai: Removal takes a supermajority of all serving members — the same bar for everyone, in any office. Removal parity means no office is easier to remove from than another.
education_legislature_oversight.s3_detai: When a seat empties it is declared, and the count is re-run from the original ballots rather than a new election being called.
education_legislature_oversight.why: the countback is universal — every prior ballot counts, with no filtering anywhere in the procedure. The voters who elected the chamber decide the replacement.
education_legislature_overview.learn: One legislature in context: its jurisdiction, its districts, its seats and its term.
education_legislature_overview.s1_detail: Seats are apportioned across the districts that make it up.
education_legislature_overview.s2_detail: Terms and intervals come from the settings register, inside constitutional bounds.
education_legislature_overview.s2_do: See its term and next election
education_legislature_referendums.learn: When the legislature hands a decision back to the people, and what happens to the result.
education_legislature_referendums.s1_det: The chamber can put a question to the jurisdiction.
education_legislature_referendums.s1_do: See what has been delegated to a vote
education_legislature_referendums.s2_det: Derived from the act type, never editable. Whoever writes the referendum cannot also choose how hard it is to pass.
education_legislature_referendums.s3_det: A referendum act can be modified or repealed — but only by a route the constitution fixes, not by ordinary rewriting.
education_legislature_referendums.s3_do: See how a result can be changed
education_legislature_session_console.le: A meeting while it is happening — attendance, quorum, the agenda, and every vote as it is cast.
education_legislature_session_console.s1: Presence is recorded per member, per session.
education_legislature_session_console.s2: Quorum is a majority of all serving members — not of whoever turned up. Empty chairs count against it.
education_legislature_session_console.s3: Motions, statements for the record, and floor votes all happen here and all land on the permanent record.
education_legislature_session_console.wh: counting against all serving members is the whole trick. It means absence can never shrink the bar — you cannot pass something by emptying the room.
education_legislature_settings.learn: The dials a legislature is allowed to turn, the bounds they must stay inside, and the ones nobody can turn at all.
education_legislature_settings.s1_detail: Election intervals, thresholds, term lengths — the amendable layer.
education_legislature_settings.s2_detail: Settings move by ordinary act, inside locked bounds.
education_legislature_settings.s2_do: Change one by passing a bill
education_legislature_settings.s3_detail: An out-of-range value is rejected before the vote is even taken — you cannot pass an unconstitutional setting and argue later.
education_legislature_settings.why: there are exactly two doors. Settings move by ordinary acts within fixed bounds; the hardened core changes only by a software release that passes the public constitutional checks. There is no third door, and no majority anywhere can open one.
education_legislature_speaker_tools.lear: What the Speaker can actually do — which is less than most people assume.
education_legislature_speaker_tools.s1_d: Call sessions and set the agenda
education_legislature_speaker_tools.s2_d: Both are public acts, not internal bookkeeping.
education_legislature_speaker_tools.s3_d: The Speaker does not hold an ordinary vote. The casting vote exists solely to resolve a deadlock.
Break a tie — and only a tie
education_legislature_speaker_tools.s4_d: The Speaker chairs impeachment and censure proceedings; the chamber votes.
Preside over a removal, never decide it
education_legislature_speaker_tools.why: the chair runs the room, it does not rule it. Every power here is procedural.
education_operator_console.learn: The controls for the node you run, and the acts that are logged when you use them.
education_operator_console.s2_detail: Operator acts are logged as operator acts. They are never constitutional filings and never enter the governance chain.
education_operator_console.s2_do: Note what is on the operator plane, not the constitutional one
education_operator_dns.learn: The Identity Broker gives peers their names and the certificates that prove those names — how a node proves it is itself. It is the heaviest thing an operator can do, because naming a peer touches that peer's own corner of the mesh.
education_operator_dns.s1_detail: The token that lets the broker write name records is stored encrypted and write-only — set once, never shown again, never logged, and leaves this box only as a sealed copy for a failover broker you designate. The broker uses it; nothing ever reads it back.
education_operator_dns.s1_do: Register a domain and set its write token once
education_operator_dns.s2_detail: The broker points the name at your address before it asks the free certificate authority (Let's Encrypt) for the proof, with a budget check in between — the authority allows only so many attempts a week (50 per domain, 5 per exact name), so a refusal arrives with a fix and costs nothing.
education_operator_dns.s2_do: Write the name first, the certificate second
education_operator_dns.s3_detail: One certificate for exactly one name is the default and the only ungated path today. Wildcard certificates and the non-Cloudflare automated providers are not built yet; the Manual provider always works — it hands you the exact record to set by hand.
education_operator_dns.s4_detail: Writing names under a domain, or minting grants, can act inside another peer's area. Those channels wait for the affected peers' own consent — on top of any approval vote. Naming is a capability, never a rank: it buys no vote, seat, or say.
education_operator_dns.s4_do: Note when a peer must say yes
education_operator_home.learn: Running a node — the volunteer servers the world runs on. Keeping it online buys no vote and no seat.
education_operator_home.s1_detail: Health, storage, and what it is serving.
education_operator_home.s2_detail: Operating the infrastructure confers no governance power whatsoever.
education_operator_home.why: whoever holds the keys always could be powerful. So the app puts nothing behind that door — no role, no vote, no seat — and says so out loud on the operator's own home screen.
education_operator_identity.learn: How this instance proves it is itself to the rest of the mesh.
education_operator_identity.s1_detail: Identity is how Full Faith and Credit works — a peer must know whose record it is trusting.
education_operator_identity.s1_do: See the node's identity and keys
education_operator_identity.s2_detail: Node identity is not any person's identity.
education_operator_mesh.learn: Which other instances this node talks to, and how.
education_operator_mesh.s1_detail: Federation is between whole governments, not between users.
education_operator_mesh.s2_detail: Public records and earned achievements travel. Ballots, envelopes, education progress and the private social graph never do.
education_operator_mesh.s2_do: Note what crosses and what does not
education_operator_moderation.learn: You host the rooms; you never judge the speech. This screen shows the only four constitutional reasons a post can ever be removed — plus the separate real-world legal floor, who may act on each — and how that authority moves to a judge, automatically, the moment a government exists.
education_operator_moderation.s1_detail: A judicial order, protecting another person's rights, your own personal block, and content-neutral anti-spam. There is no fifth carve-out — a "remove for content" control has no code path, so no one can be pressured into using one. Every server-side removal is logged; your personal block is not a removal at all — it filters only your own screen and is never recorded.
education_operator_moderation.s2_detail: Before any legislature is seated, the operator board relays a rights-protection removal — neutral, logged, and marked so it can never be mistaken for a judge's ruling. The board relays; it never rules.
education_operator_moderation.s2_do: Relay while there is no government
education_operator_moderation.s3_detail: The moment a legislature seats itself, only a seated judge may order a judicial or rights-protection removal, and the operator relay stops being honored. Nobody flips a switch — the change is a pure function of the facts.
education_operator_moderation.s3_do: Let the flip happen on its own
education_operator_moderation.s4_detail: Already-posted illegal material — a known illegal-image match, a specific court order, a true threat — is removed under the law of the country the server physically sits in. The list is closed and grows only by code release; each act is per item, never a standing filter; the sealed evidence trail is append-only.
education_operator_moderation.s4_do: Apply the legal floor when real-world law compels it
education_operator_moderation.why: an operator could always pull the plug — that is physics. So the code gives the operator no verb for censorship: the removal form exists only for the two office-gated reasons — your block and anti-spam never touch a form at all, every use lands in the permanent record, and the moment a real government exists even the relay authority evaporates. The guarantee is not the operator's virtue — it is the absence of the control.
education_operator_roles.learn: Trust between nodes, expressed as specific capabilities rather than blanket authority.
education_operator_roles.s1_detail: Trust is composable — a peer trusted for one channel is not trusted for all.
education_operator_roles.s1_do: See what each peer is trusted for
education_operator_roles.s2_detail: Each is a separate, reversible decision.
education_operator_setup.learn: Five steps take a bare box to a live node on the mesh: claim an operator account, name the instance, pick what the node will do, run its setup, go. None of it buys a vote, a seat, or any say — running a node is infrastructure, not power.
education_operator_setup.s1_detail: Your password works on this box only. Other boxes recognise you by possession of a device key — only the public half ever enrols, and no password is ever replayed between boxes.
education_operator_setup.s2_detail: The name is a friendly label; the self-URL is the address peers dial to sync with you. A stable server id is minted on first run and survives any rename.
education_operator_setup.s3_detail: Record Keeper — holding a copy of the public record — is the one role you switch on yourself, one click, no approval. Once a mesh or a seated government exists, everything else this wizard can only request: approval comes from the operator board while no legislature is seated, from the seated government itself the moment one exists — and peers whose own area is touched must consent too.
education_operator_setup.s3_do: Pick what your node will do
education_operator_setup.s4_detail: Operator accounts have no link to citizen accounts, and nothing you enable here changes what any citizen can do. Voting and candidacy flow from residency alone — a server room grants neither.
education_operator_setup.s4_do: Know what this buys you: nothing
education_operator_setup.why: the one-click role is the one that gives you no power over anyone — keeping a copy of a record every peer already holds. Every capability that touches other people (serving them, naming them, hosting their rooms) must be granted from outside the box. Once a mesh or a seated government exists, the machine's owner cannot self-grant.
education_operator_versioning.learn: Which version of the constitutional code this instance is running, and why that is a public fact.
education_operator_versioning.s1_detail: The hardened core lives in code, so which code is a constitutional fact.
education_operator_versioning.s2_detail: This is the only route by which hardened rules change — a release that passes the public constitutional checks.
How an organization's board is chosen — and why some seats are elected by workers.
Owner-elected and worker-elected seats sit on the same board.
See the seats and their classes
Owner and worker elections are administered separately by the agent.
The chair is classless — the joint chair belongs to neither side.
education_organizations_cgc_detail.learn: A company chartered to serve the public — and the one rule that makes it different from every other company.
education_organizations_cgc_detail.s1_de: Created by an act of a legislature, to serve a public purpose.
education_organizations_cgc_detail.s2_de: Everything a CGC creates — patents, trade secrets, copyrighted works — is universally and eternally in the public domain.
education_organizations_cgc_detail.s3_de: That status is permanent. It cannot be sold, licensed away, or reversed by any later act.
education_organizations_cgc_detail.why: this is the sharpest single clause in the constitution. A public-purpose company's work belongs to everyone, forever, with no mechanism anywhere to privatise it.
