education_organizations_co_determination: The rule that gives the people who do the work a share of the decisions — and how it scales with headcount.
See the current headcount and what it earns
At 2,000 employees, worker and shareholder representation reach parity.
The scale is recalculated on a clock as headcount changes. Nobody has to remember to apply it.
this is automatic, and that is the point. Co-determination that depends on an owner choosing to grant it is not co-determination.
education_organizations_org_detail.learn: One organization's public face — ownership, board, endorsements, and how to join.
education_organizations_org_detail.s2_de: A candidate requests (F-CAN-002); the agent grants (F-ORG-002), which is forced public and confers R-07 on the candidate.
education_organizations_org_detail.s3_de: Membership and work are separate paths with separate consequences.
education_organizations_org_detail.s3_do: Join, or register as a worker
education_organizations_org_detail.why: endorsement linkage feeds proportionality, never a faction layer. The worker headcount feeds the co-determination scale. One organization model carries both.
education_organizations_org_registry.lea: Every registered organization where you live — parties, businesses, nonprofits and public companies, in one open list.
education_organizations_org_registry.s1_: One registry, one model, discriminated only by type. There is no faction layer.
education_organizations_org_registry.s3_: Endorsement, not membership, is the political-linkage metric.
education_organizations_transfers_conver: Changing who owns an organization, or changing what kind of thing it is.
A filed act, on the record.
Conversion changes the rules that apply — including, for a CGC, the permanent public-domain status of what it has already created.
Dissolution is also a public act.
Dissolve, if that is the end
education_shared_accessibility.learn: Representation for every one of us means an interface every one of us can operate — across ability, language, script direction, device, and connection. This statement records what is built in, what is honestly unfinished, and where to report the difference.
education_shared_accessibility.s1_detail: Keyboard for every interaction, visible focus everywhere, AA contrast, reflow to small screens and 400% zoom, reduced-motion support, right-to-left mirroring. If a screen falls short of this list, that is a defect — not a preference.
education_shared_accessibility.s1_do: Hold the interface to the contract
education_shared_accessibility.s2_detail: What is not done yet is listed rather than hidden — so you know the difference between a gap that is scheduled and one that nobody has noticed.
education_shared_accessibility.s3_detail: Accessibility is one of the six report subjects, and a report routes itself to the people who fix design defects. You need no status, role, or account standing to file one.
education_shared_accessibility.why: Voting and candidacy require nothing beyond living in the place you vote in. An interface a person cannot operate would quietly add a requirement the constitution forbids — which is why an accessibility defect here is a constitutional defect, not polish. | Art. I
education_shared_atlas.learn: The Atlas is the public heartbeat of the whole game — one breathing map plus the vital signs of representation, justice, the economy, and the servers carrying it all. Everything on it is an aggregate; it never shows a person who has not chosen to appear.
education_shared_atlas.s1_detail: Nodes, places, organizations, and opt-in residents — at city-level, approximate positions, with layers you can switch off. This is orientation, not surveillance.
education_shared_atlas.s2_detail: Appearing is strictly opt-in: one approximate dot, snapped to a grid, no name attached, removable. Your residency pings are a different thing entirely — private, never published, and never on this map.
education_shared_atlas.s2_do: Put yourself on the map — or don't
education_shared_atlas.s3_detail: Seats filled and open, elections and candidates, cases and juries, stipends and market volume — every number comes off the engine, aggregated. Reach is a display-only transparency gauge: never a governance input, never a per-person score.
education_shared_atlas.s4_detail: Open seats and open elections list what needs people right now. Anyone resident may stand — the Atlas shows you the door and adds no gate in front of it.
education_shared_atlas.why: The map draws the line the whole system keeps: participation is celebrated in aggregate, but no individual is ever ranked, scored, or located. A jurisdiction may have a leaderboard; a person never does.
education_shared_constitutional_question: Building a constitution into working software forces decisions the text never made — and this ledger keeps every one of them on the record: the question, the answer the build chose, and where to watch that answer working.

Each names the constitutional text it touches, what the attempt to build it surfaced, and the implemented answer in one paragraph — with links to the screens where the answer is visible, so you can judge it in action.
Every such marker across the app resolves to its anchor here. An interpretive choice is never silent — you can always trace a behavior back to the question that produced it.

Entries are appended as new questions surface; existing ones are only ever extended, never rewritten. Changing the running system itself goes through the amendment doors — this page is the honest margin note beside them, and it seeds the next draft of the constitution.
Watch the ledger grow — never shrink

Software that implements a constitution holds interpretive power, and the honest response is to write every use of it down in public. The ledger is that confession — permanent, appended-only, and addressed to the people who will redraft the text.
education_shared_launchpad.learn: The front door of the whole world — four ways in, eight kinds of live room, and a directory of journeys that teach by doing. Nothing at this door checks who you are; every path on this page is open to whoever walks up.
education_shared_launchpad.s1_detail: The four doors are the real arrivals: a friend's invite, what's happening today where you live, the living Atlas, or straight into a live room. None of them asks for an account first.
education_shared_launchpad.s2_detail: Eight kinds of meeting share one familiar door — committee, chamber, an executive's table, courtroom, board, forum, town hall, a circle of friends. Public bodies are always open to watch; a private group decides its own visibility.
education_shared_launchpad.s3_detail: Each journey walks you through one real thing this world does — what's happening now, what's your part, what happens next — passing through real rooms along the way. Finish one and you earn an achievement you can show on your profile; it grants nothing else — no vote, no seat, no capability.
education_shared_launchpad.s4_detail: Underneath, every journey is one of five kinds of interaction. That map is for later, once you've been here a while — it is never a prerequisite for anything.
education_shared_tour.learn: The tour is a mode, not a place — one linear path through every screen, with a Back / Next bar riding on top of the real thing. Enter anywhere, leave any time; walking it changes nothing about your rights or your standing.
education_shared_tour.s1_detail: The short track follows the way a real arrival goes: a friend's invite, a live room, home, the living world, your first ballot. About ten minutes.
education_shared_tour.s2_detail: Every stop is the real screen, fully usable — not a slideshow copy of it. The tour just adds Back / Next on top, so you can wander off inside a stop and still find your way.
education_shared_tour.s3_detail: Use the normal menu at any moment and the tour simply falls away; come back to this index for the full list. Finishing the tour grants nothing — no role, no vote, no capability — and skipping it costs nothing either.
education_social_achievements.learn: Your earned records — civic firsts and finished journeys — kept as a list, never a score. Nothing on this page grants anything: no vote, no seat, no role, no eligibility, ever.
education_social_achievements.s1_detail: Verified achievements are written by the system when the permanent record shows the act — a filing, a seating, a confirmation. Achievements about voting read only the sealed envelope that proves you took part; the ballot inside is never opened.
education_social_achievements.s1_do: Earn by doing, not by claiming
education_social_achievements.s2_detail: Verified entries are proven by the server's own records. Walkthrough entries come from guided journeys and are self-reported ticks — they are labeled as walkthroughs precisely so they cannot borrow the verified tier's credibility.
education_social_achievements.s2_do: Read the tier label on each one
education_social_achievements.s3_detail: Your achievements are private until you choose to show them, and your progress meters are worked out from your own activity when you look — never kept as a stored score. Shown or hidden, nothing changes.
education_social_achievements.s4_detail: Finishing a training pays a stipend bonus exactly once. The "once" is enforced right here: this ledger can only ever gain an entry, so an achievement is earned once — and the bonus that reads it can never pay twice.
education_social_achievements.s4_do: Take the one-time completion bonus when it applies
education_social_achievements.why: The service that writes this page refuses to count. It returns which achievements you hold, never how many — a completion percentage is a per-person score wearing a different hat. Jurisdictions may celebrate milestones together; people are never ranked against each other. And no gate anywhere consults this list: standing for office needs residency, and nothing else.
education_social_profile.learn: Every person — you, a neighbour, a candidate, the holder of your seat — is shown by this same tabbed profile. Which tabs are public is decided by the constitution, not by rank: there is no separate kind of profile for officials.
education_social_profile.s1_detail: A handle is the default; showing your legal name is a choice you make, and either way you hold exactly the same rights. A pseudonym is a first-class way to live a civic life.
education_social_profile.s2_detail: The Record tab is the audited civic history: residency, participation, offices, filings. It shows that a person voted, never how — and it can only ever be added to, never quietly edited.
education_social_profile.s3_detail: A person standing for election gains a Candidacy tab; a person holding a seat gains an Office tab. Those tabs are public because seeking and holding public power is public — the rest of their life is not.
education_social_profile.s3_do: Meet candidacies and offices as tabs, not identities
education_social_profile.s4_detail: Following someone, messaging them, or reaching a representative never costs anything and never requires joining anything. Endorsements you see here are public only because each endorser chose to say so.
education_social_profile.why: The public/private line on this page is drawn by the constitution, not by the person's importance. Candidacy statements are public and every edit lands on the record; office records and every act taken in office are public and uneditable; groups, wallet, and whom you follow stay private. And the public parts inform — an endorsement, however grand, never gates a single thing.
education_support_report.learn: When something is wrong — a broken page, a mistranslation, an accessibility barrier, abuse — this is the one door. You pick the subject; the report finds the right people on its own.
education_support_report.s1_detail: Something is broken, wording or translation, an accessibility barrier, wrong information, abuse or illegal content, or an idea. A complaint about someone's conduct files under abuse. Your choice is the routing — bugs and barriers go to the operators, wording to the translators, ideas to the backlog.
education_support_report.s1_do: Pick one of the six categories
education_support_report.s2_detail: What you expected, and what you saw instead. The page you were on and the software version attach themselves — you never have to explain where you were. You file from your account, but you don't have to use your real name, and where you live is never attached.
education_support_report.s3_detail: The report becomes a numbered ticket you can watch move from new to resolved in the ticket queue.
education_support_report.s4_detail: An abuse or illegal-content report skips the tech-support queue and goes straight to the moderation and legal team — and even they never judge viewpoint. Content comes down only through the logged removal paths — a judicial order, protecting another's rights, your own block, or content-neutral anti-spam. Support staff never decide what people may say.
education_support_report.why: Notice the subject that is not on the list: appealing a decision. Challenging a ruling or an official act is constitutional business — it belongs before the courts (Art. IV), never a help desk. Support fixes the software; it holds no power over what anyone did with it.
education_support_ticket.learn: One report from filing to resolution: what was said, where it routed, and every status change since — a living thread you can add to.
education_support_ticket.s1_detail: The number, status, severity, and category, plus who reported it, where it routed, and the page it happened on. When a report isn't tech-support business the ticket says so plainly — abuse sits with the moderation and legal team, and a translation issue lives in that language's review queue, where readers of the language verify the fix.
education_support_ticket.s2_detail: Every event carries who acted, when, and what changed — new, triaged, in progress, resolved. The routing happens on the record, not behind a desk.
education_support_ticket.s2_do: Follow the status and history thread
education_support_ticket.s3_detail: A reply with more detail or a way to reproduce the problem can be the difference between "can't reproduce" and fixed.
education_support_ticket.s4_detail: Your +1 tells the people triaging how widespread the problem is. It is a signal of reach, not a vote — nothing here is decided by popularity.
education_support_tickets.learn: Every report filed and where it stands — nothing vanishes into a private inbox. Filter it, follow your own, and add weight to the problems that hit you too.
education_support_tickets.s1_detail: "Open" covers new, triaged, and in progress; resolved, closed, and won't fix are the finished states. Subject narrows the list to bugs, wording, accessibility, wrong information, abuse, or ideas.
education_support_tickets.s2_detail: The number, a severity dot, the title, its status, the category it routed under, how many people said it affects them, and when it last moved.
education_support_tickets.s2_do: Read a row at a glance
education_support_tickets.s3_detail: Each row opens the full report with its history thread. The report button stays in reach for anything you hit that isn't listed yet.
education_support_tickets.s3_do: Open a ticket — or file a new one
education_system_amendments.learn: The constitution changes through exactly two doors: settings move by ordinary acts within locked bounds, and the hardened core changes only by a software release that passes the public constitutional checks.
education_system_amendments.s1_detail: The settings register, inside fixed bounds.
education_system_amendments.s2_detail: The counting method, the supermajority formula, the rights gates. No majority anywhere can move these by act.
education_system_amendments.s3_detail: Anything that is not one of these two is not a route.
education_system_amendments.s3_do: Note there is no third door
education_system_audit_chain.learn: The audit chain — every constitutional act, hash-chained in order. Anyone can verify that nothing was quietly changed.
education_system_audit_chain.s1_detail: Every filing — accepted and rejected — is an entry, in order.
education_system_audit_chain.s2_detail: Each entry carries the hash of the one before it. Changing any past entry breaks every entry after it.
education_system_audit_chain.s3_detail: Ballot contents are never chained. Participation is recorded; how you voted is not.
education_system_audit_chain.s3_do: Note what is not in it
education_system_audit_chain.why: tamper-evidence, not tamper-proofing. Nobody claims the past cannot be altered — the claim is that altering it cannot be hidden.
education_system_clocks.learn: The scheduled sweeps that drive the world — every interval, deadline, window, and threshold that starts a process without anyone asking. Clocks hold no state; they move other things.
education_system_clocks.s1_detail: Twenty-one clocks, each with a stated cadence and a stated effect.
education_system_clocks.s2_detail: The emergency-powers clock cannot be extended past ninety days by any act.
education_system_clocks.s2_do: Note the ones with constitutional ceilings
education_system_clocks.s3_detail: A deadline that depends on someone remembering is not a deadline.
education_system_public_records.learn: The permanent public record — testimony, votes, acts, and rulings, readable by anyone, editable by no one.
education_system_public_records.s2_detai: Ballots, envelopes, location pings and the private social graph are structurally barred from publication — refused at the single point where anything gets published.
education_system_public_records.s2_do: Note what may never enter it
education_system_term_sync.learn: Why civil and judicial appointment terms move together, and why that matters.
education_system_term_sync.s1_detail: Both ten years, and they must stay in lockstep.
education_system_term_sync.s2_detail: Changing one without the other is refused.
education_system_term_sync.why: if one branch's terms could be shortened alone, whoever controlled that lever could time appointments to their advantage. Locking them together removes the lever.
education_system_translation_review.lear: One language, one page: how much of the world reads in it, what the machine has drafted, and what its own readers have verified. Machine and human work are never confused — a draft stays marked as a draft until people who read the language agree it is right.
education_system_translation_review.s1_d: Interface text, page copy, guide audio, captions — each shows its own progress bar and verifier count for this language, so you can put your effort where it moves the most.
education_system_translation_review.s2_d: Each one shows the English source beside the machine's first draft, worst-off first — including strings the machine itself refused to ship. Accept a good draft or suggest a better wording.
education_system_translation_review.s3_d: A string becomes community-verified only when enough readers of the language agree. Verification is gated to the people who actually read it — never a central team, and never the machine grading itself.
education_system_translation_review.s4_d: Form, role, clock, and workflow codes (F-…, R-…, CLK-…, WF-…) are never translated. They stay identical in every language, so a citation means exactly the same thing everywhere on Earth.

learn.q.chamber_basics.q1.prompt: A chamber has 12 serving members and 2 vacant seats. How many members must be present for quorum?
learn.q.chamber_basics.q1.a: Seven — a majority of whoever attended the last session
learn.q.chamber_basics.q1.b: Seven — a majority of ALL serving members
learn.q.chamber_basics.q1.c: Eight — two-thirds of the serving members
learn.q.chamber_basics.q1.explain: Quorum is a majority of ALL serving members (Art. II §2). Vacant seats are not serving members, and past attendance never enters the arithmetic.
learn.q.chamber_basics.q2.prompt: What does a supermajority act require?
learn.q.chamber_basics.q2.a: Two-thirds of the members present and voting
learn.q.chamber_basics.q2.b: Two-thirds of members present, once quorum has formed
learn.q.chamber_basics.q2.c: Two-thirds of ALL serving members — a member who stays away counts the same as a no
learn.q.chamber_basics.q2.explain: Art. VII counts the whole serving roster, never just the room. That is why absence can never be used to cheapen a supermajority.
learn.q.chamber_basics.q3.prompt: How is your vote on a bill actually cast?
learn.q.chamber_basics.q3.a: By filing the floor-vote form (F-LEG-004) — every chamber vote is a public act on the record
learn.q.chamber_basics.q3.b: By telling the speaker, who records the tally
learn.q.chamber_basics.q3.c: By secret ballot, like an election
learn.q.chamber_basics.q3.explain: Chamber votes are public constitutional acts — F-LEG-004 on the audit chain. Ballot secrecy protects ELECTIONS; representation is exercised in the open.
learn.q.running_elections.q1.prompt: Which counting method do elections use?
learn.q.running_elections.q1.a: Proportional STV with the Droop quota — never first-past-the-post
learn.q.running_elections.q1.b: Whoever gets the most votes wins
learn.q.running_elections.q1.c: Whatever method the board prefers for that election
learn.q.running_elections.q1.explain: Art. II §2 hard-codes STV with the Droop quota. It can only ever be replaced by a MORE proportional method — never by plurality.
learn.q.running_elections.q2.prompt: How many seats may a single district race carry?
learn.q.running_elections.q2.a: Any number the map drawer likes
learn.q.running_elections.q2.b: Five to nine — a legislature above nine seats subdivides into districts
learn.q.running_elections.q2.explain: The 5–9 band is a DISTRICT rule (Art. II §2). A chamber's TOTAL has no ceiling — Earth seats 1,999 across 282 districts.
learn.q.running_elections.q3.prompt: What actually seats the winners after a count?
learn.q.running_elections.q3.b: The board's certification (F-ELB-004) — seating follows it automatically
learn.q.running_elections.q3.explain: Certification is the constitutional act; auto-seating rides it. The oath (F-LEG-001) accepts a seat certification already created.
learn.q.executive_basics.q1.prompt: How does a new executive normally begin?
learn.q.executive_basics.q1.c: Delegated by the legislature — direct election comes later, and only by supermajority
learn.q.executive_basics.q1.explain: Art. III: every executive starts legislature-delegated. Converting to direct election takes a dual supermajority — the chamber's and the constituents'.
learn.q.executive_basics.q2.prompt: What must happen before an executive order takes effect?
learn.q.executive_basics.q2.a: Its scope is validated against the office's delegated powers — before issuance, not after
learn.q.executive_basics.q2.b: Nothing — orders are immediate and unreviewable
learn.q.executive_basics.q2.explain: F-EXE-005 runs pre-issuance scope validation. An order outside the delegated scope is refused with its citation, not issued and litigated later.
learn.q.executive_basics.q3.prompt: Emergency powers can last at most…
learn.q.executive_basics.q3.a: As long as the emergency lasts
learn.q.executive_basics.q3.b: 90 days per declaration or renewal — and expiry is automatic
learn.q.executive_basics.q3.explain: Art. II §7 sets the 90-day ceiling; CLK-03 expires them automatically. Renewal of an already-expired power is refused.
learn.q.department_basics.q1.prompt: How long is a governor's appointment?
learn.q.department_basics.q1.b: Ten years — in lockstep with judicial appointments
learn.q.department_basics.q1.explain: Civil and judicial appointments share the ten-year term (Art. II §9, Art. IV §1) and move in lockstep — neither can drift alone.
learn.q.department_basics.q2.prompt: A department rule you implement (F-BOG-001) must…
learn.q.department_basics.q2.a: Stay inside the department's delegated scope
learn.q.department_basics.q2.c: Be countersigned by every governor on the board
learn.q.department_basics.q2.explain: A department implements within the scope its creation act delegated. Outside that scope, the rule is refused with its citation.
learn.q.bench_basics.q1.c: Appointed — a judiciary is appointed by default, for ten years
learn.q.bench_basics.q1.explain: Art. IV §1: appointed is the default, ten-year terms, at least five judges per race. Switching to an elected bench needs a supermajority plus a constituent supermajority.
learn.q.bench_basics.q2.a: Odd-sized, at least three judges — scaled to the case's severity
learn.q.bench_basics.q2.explain: Panels are odd and at least three (Art. IV §4), scaling with severity; a constitutional-major case takes the whole court en banc.
learn.q.bench_basics.q3.prompt: Can a person be tried twice for the same matter?
learn.q.bench_basics.q3.b: No — double jeopardy is barred at the filing gate itself
learn.q.bench_basics.q3.explain: The second filing is refused before any case opens — the bar lives at the validator, not in a judge's discretion.
learn.q.advocacy_basics.q1.prompt: Filing a case for a client uses…
learn.q.advocacy_basics.q1.a: F-ADV-001 — the advocate files on the client's behalf, on the record
learn.q.advocacy_basics.q1.b: A private letter to the presiding judge
learn.q.advocacy_basics.q1.explain: F-ADV-001 opens a case on a client's behalf; everything an advocate does is a filed, citable act on the docket.
learn.q.advocacy_basics.q2.prompt: Motions, evidence and briefs may be filed…
learn.q.advocacy_basics.q2.c: Inside the case's attach window, onto the docket
learn.q.advocacy_basics.q2.explain: F-ADV-002/003/004 ride the attach-window gate — the docket is complete when the window closes, so nobody is ambushed at the bench.
